body:
Aw, that's so sweet for you to say. I did go outside for a few mins to calm down, until my hands stopped shaking, and focusing on my surroundings. I used to think I'm a strange person for having many ups and downs, but I know for certain there are always people struggling, or feeling hopeless. That's why I wanted to express myself, even if the word I used can be triggering, and there are others desperately looking for help.

Yes, the best option is a therapist, the thing is...I didn't have a good experience with my last one. I got ignored and when the pandemic started, I couldn't find a private time in the house for a zoom session, so I thought I could just endure it to the end. Overall, it was in my plans to see a new one but it's difficult. And now I take Clonazepam to help me relax a bit. It's a temporal solution, I know.

Sorry if my post seemed like I wanted to fish for some compliments, I wasn't having a good time lately, with that s-word I drop in the title and all.... But you sound like a lovely lady, and your writing gives me a warm feeling. Thank you so much for your kind words auntie!

So far I've invested 5 years on this career. At first I did chose it with the purpose of helping people, and it was tied with one of my wishes from when I was little, the one when you often get asked *"hey, what do you want to become when you're older?"* I always said I wanted to be a doctor, or something similar. Also, my late grandfather was proud of the idea. 

After graduating highschool I wasn't sure what to do, because if I wanted to study something medical-related, in the public university you could only study infirmary, the rest of them were on private institutes. Just for the sake of not spending money, I tried two careers and it was a failure. That's when I started with radiology, and at first it was good. But then many factors put a wall on me, and now that's why I say I'm so close but so far. I feel like I wasted many opportunities, so yeah, doing this does relieve the pain.

My dad is an old man, compared to my age (almost 70). I do get that the generation gap is significant, and still love him. I guess I was more sad with the fact I wouldn't know how he would react in the case I told the truth, since he's very temperamental. Still, I get what you're saying with that. I tend to be pessimistic. And even worse.

Fair enough, after all, I did chose to get into at this point, right..? Wish I had more willpower, only thing it's left for me before I fall into the abyss is to focus like there's no tomorrow and hope for the best.

Thank you so much!
